title: The effects of deep brain stimulation on the cognitive symptoms of Parkinson's disease
summary:
Parkinson’s disease is best known for its movement problems, such as tremor and stiffness. But many people with the disease also experience cognitive difficulties. They may have trouble concentrating, struggle to find words, or have memory problems. These cognitive symptoms are often particularly distressing for patients and their families, and so far there are only a few treatment options for them.

Many people with Parkinson’s disease are treated with deep brain stimulation (DBS), also known as a brain pacemaker. This implanted device sends electrical impulses to a specific brain region (the subthalamic nucleus), which is very effective in relieving movement problems. Normally, the device operates at high frequencies (about 130 Hz). It has been suggested that stimulation at low frequencies (6-12 Hz) might improve cognitive function.

With this study, we would like to test this possibility systematically. To do so, we plan to carry out cognitive tests with 50 people with Parkinson’s disease who have an implanted brain pacemaker. These include a memory task in which two sequences of numbers are presented one after the other, and participants must decide whether the two sequences are identical. They also include a word fluency task, in which participants have a limited amount of time to name as many words as possible that belong to a given category (e.g., animals) or begin with a given letter. Finally, we will also measure motor function: participants tap their index finger as many times as possible within a set time. All tasks are performed under three experimental conditions: 1) stimulation at 6 Hz, 2) stimulation at 130 Hz, and 3) stimulation switched off. We hypothesize that stimulation at 6 Hz will improve cognitive performance, whereas stimulation at 130 Hz will improve motor function.

In a subset of participants (at least 20), we will record brain activity during the tasks using magnetoencephalography (MEG) in order to understand how the stimulation affects the brain.

interventions.name: Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus at 6 Hz, applied for the duration of the tasks (about 30 min)
Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus at 130 Hz, applied for the duration of the tasks (about 30 min)
Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus switched off for the duration of the tasks (about 30 min)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All participants must be over 18 years of age and capable of giving informed consent. Patients must have a diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease in accordance with the guideline and be treated with deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus.
Exclusion criteria:
People with dementia or other conditions that significantly affect cognition cannot take part in the study.
